title: Rav Chinena bar Kahana
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He was Rav’s student, as in Rosh Hashanah 19b and Beitzah 6a: “Rav Chinena bar Kahana said that Rav said: From the days of Ezra onward we have not found Elul intercalated.” In Beitzah 22b and Rosh Hashanah 32a the words “that Rav said” are missing. In Avodah Zarah 20b he said: “In the school of Rav they say: One who wants his dead not to decay should turn him on his face.”

We likewise find “Rav Chinena bar Kahana said that Shmuel said,” as in Ketubot 65a and 72a and Bava Kamma 113b (there Rav Chanina bar Kahana), and in Shmuel’s name in Taanit 30a. Likewise “Rav Chinena bar Kahana said that Rav Assi said,” as in Eruvin 55a (Hyman proposes this reading, regarding “Rav Ashi” as a printing error and reporting Rav Assi in Venice). In Shabbat 96a he spoke in Rabbi Elazar’s name (Hyman proposes Elazar, not Rabbi Eliezer — Dikdukei Soferim). He is mentioned in Sanhedrin 70a: “Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana said: Salted meat, so long as it is like shelamim,” etc.

notes.text: The Assi/Ashi and Elazar/Eliezer choices are Hyman’s stated textual corrections, not blanket normalization. The Sanhedrin salted-meat statement is abridged as supplied.

Rosh Hashanah 19b directly names Rabbi Chinena bar Kahana reporting Rav; the Rav/Rabbi forms remain as supplied in each source. The bounded Eruvin 55a comparison did not locate the cited Assi transmission. Hyman’s Venice and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain attributed to him; those exact editions were not independently inspected.
